Most example code taken from Oracle Java Documentation, which is an excellent reference for Java. If you're new to Java, read that documentation. Seriously.

Java in a Nutshell ​

  • Object-oriented programming language
  • Statically typed with type inference for local variables (Java 10+)
  • Platform-independent ("Write Once, Run Anywhere")
  • Automatic memory management via garbage collection
  • Strong type system with generics
  • Rich standard library
  • Multi-threading support
  • Exception handling mechanism
  • Reflection capabilities

Basic Syntax ​

Hello World ​

File HelloWorld.java:

java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, World!");
    }
}

$ javac HelloWorld.java && java HelloWorld

Variables and Data Types ​

java
// Primitive types
byte b = 127;        // 8-bit signed integer
short s = 32767;     // 16-bit signed integer
int i = 2147483647;  // 32-bit signed integer
long l = 9223372036854775807L; // 64-bit signed integer

float f = 3.14f;     // 32-bit floating point
double d = 3.14159;  // 64-bit floating point

char c = 'A';        // 16-bit Unicode character
boolean flag = true; // true or false

// Reference types
String str = "Hello";
int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};

// Type inference with var (Java 10+)
var name = "John";   // String
var age = 30;        // int
var list = new ArrayList<String>(); // ArrayList<String>

// Constants
final double PI = 3.14159;

Methods ​

java
public class Calculator {
    // Static method
    public static int add(int a, int b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    
    // Instance method
    public double multiply(double a, double b) {
        return a * b;
    }
    
    // Method with variable arguments (varargs)
    public int sum(int... numbers) {
        int total = 0;
        for (int num : numbers) {
            total += num;
        }
        return total;
    }
    
    // Method overloading
    public int add(int a, int b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    
    public double add(double a, double b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    
    // Main method - entry point
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int result = add(5, 3);
        System.out.println("Result: " + result);
    }
}

Control Flow ​

if/else ​

java
int score = 85;

if (score >= 90) {
    System.out.println("A");
} else if (score >= 80) {
    System.out.println("B");
} else if (score >= 70) {
    System.out.println("C");
} else {
    System.out.println("F");
}

// Ternary operator
String grade = (score >= 80) ? "Pass" : "Fail";

switch ​

java
int day = 3;
String dayName;

switch (day) {
    case 1:
        dayName = "Monday";
        break;
    case 2:
        dayName = "Tuesday";
        break;
    case 3:
        dayName = "Wednesday";
        break;
    default:
        dayName = "Unknown";
        break;
}

// Enhanced switch (Java 14+)
String dayNameEnhanced = switch (day) {
    case 1 -> "Monday";
    case 2 -> "Tuesday";
    case 3 -> "Wednesday";
    default -> "Unknown";
};

// Switch with multiple cases
String monthType;
switch (month) {
    case 1, 2, 12:
        monthType = "Winter";
        break;
    case 3, 4, 5:
        monthType = "Spring";
        break;
    case 6, 7, 8:
        monthType = "Summer";
        break;
    case 9, 10, 11:
        monthType = "Fall";
        break;
    default:
        monthType = "Unknown";
        break;
}

// Switch with expressions (Java 14+)
String monthTypeEnhanced = switch (month) {
    case 1, 2, 12 -> "Winter";
    case 3, 4, 5 -> "Spring";
    case 6, 7, 8 -> "Summer";
    case 9, 10, 11 -> "Fall";
    default -> "Unknown";
};

loops ​

java
// for loop
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    System.out.println(i);
}

// Enhanced for loop (for-each)
int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
for (int num : numbers) {
    System.out.println(num);
}

// while loop
int count = 0;
while (count < 5) {
    System.out.println(count);
    count++;
}

// do-while loop
int i = 0;
do {
    System.out.println(i);
    i++;
} while (i < 5);

// break and continue
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    if (i == 5) {
        break; // Exit the loop
    }
    if (i % 2 == 0) {
        continue; // Skip to next iteration
    }
    System.out.println(i);
}

// Labeled loops
outer:
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
        if (i == 1 && j == 1) {
            break outer; // Break out of the outer loop
        }
        System.out.println(i + ", " + j);
    }
}

Strings ​

java
// Creating strings
String str1 = "Hello";
String str2 = new String("World");
String str3 = str1 + " " + str2; // String concatenation

// String methods
int length = str1.length();
char charAt = str1.charAt(0); // 'H'
String substring = str1.substring(1, 4); // "ell"
boolean equals = str1.equals("Hello"); // true
boolean equalsIgnoreCase = str1.equalsIgnoreCase("hello"); // true
boolean contains = str1.contains("ell"); // true

String upper = str1.toUpperCase(); // "HELLO"

// String comparison
String a = "hello";
String b = new String("hello");
System.out.println(a == b); // false (different objects)
System.out.println(a.equals(b)); // true (same content)

// String formatting
String formatted = String.format("Name: %s, Age: %d", "John", 30);

// StringBuilder and StringBuffer for mutable strings
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
sb.append("Hello");
sb.append(" ");
sb.append("World");
String result = sb.toString(); // "Hello World"

StringBuffer sbuf = new StringBuffer("Thread-safe");

Collections Framework ​

List ​

java
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Collections;

// ArrayList
List<String> arrayList = new ArrayList<>();
arrayList.add("Apple");
arrayList.add("Banana");
arrayList.add("Orange");
arrayList.add(0, "Grape"); // Insert at index 0
String fruit = arrayList.get(1); // "Apple"
boolean contains = arrayList.contains("Banana"); // true
int index = arrayList.indexOf("Orange"); // 2
String removed = arrayList.remove(0); // "Grape"
int size = arrayList.size(); // 3

// LinkedList
List<Integer> linkedList = new LinkedList<>();
linkedList.add(10);
linkedList.add(20);
linkedList.add(30);
linkedList.add(1, 15); // Insert at index 1

// Utility methods
Collections.sort(arrayList); // Sort the list
Collections.reverse(arrayList); // Reverse the list
Collections.shuffle(arrayList); // Shuffle the list
int max = Collections.max(arrayList); // Find maximum element
int min = Collections.min(arrayList); // Find minimum element

// Iterating over lists
for (String item : arrayList) {
    System.out.println(item);
}

// Using Iterator
Iterator<String> iterator = arrayList.iterator();
while (iterator.hasNext()) {
    String item = iterator.next();
    System.out.println(item);
}

// Using ListIterator (bidirectional)
ListIterator<String> listIterator = arrayList.listIterator();
while (listIterator.hasNext()) {
    String item = listIterator.next();
    System.out.println(item);
}

Set ​

java
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.TreeSet;
import java.util.Set;

// HashSet (unordered, no duplicates)
Set<String> hashSet = new HashSet<>();
hashSet.add("Apple");
hashSet.add("Banana");
hashSet.add("Orange");
hashSet.add("Apple"); // Duplicate, won't be added
boolean contains = hashSet.contains("Banana"); // true
boolean removed = hashSet.remove("Orange"); // true
int size = hashSet.size(); // 2

// LinkedHashSet (maintains insertion order)
Set<String> linkedHashSet = new LinkedHashSet<>();
linkedHashSet.add("Apple");
linkedHashSet.add("Banana");
linkedHashSet.add("Orange");

// TreeSet (sorted)
Set<Integer> treeSet = new TreeSet<>();
treeSet.add(30);
treeSet.add(10);
treeSet.add(20);
treeSet.add(40);

// Iterating over sets
for (String item : hashSet) {
    System.out.println(item);
}

// Set operations
Set<String> set1 = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("A", "B", "C"));
Set<String> set2 = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("B", "C", "D"));

// Union
Set<String> union = new HashSet<>(set1);
union.addAll(set2);

// Intersection
Set<String> intersection = new HashSet<>(set1);
intersection.retainAll(set2);

// Difference
Set<String> difference = new HashSet<>(set1);
difference.removeAll(set2);

Map ​

java
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.Map;

// HashMap
Map<String, Integer> hashMap = new HashMap<>();
hashMap.put("Apple", 10);
hashMap.put("Banana", 20);
hashMap.put("Orange", 30);
int value = hashMap.get("Apple"); // 10
boolean containsKey = hashMap.containsKey("Banana"); // true
boolean containsValue = hashMap.containsValue(20); // true
int removedValue = hashMap.remove("Orange"); // 30
int size = hashMap.size(); // 2

// LinkedHashMap (maintains insertion order)
Map<String, Integer> linkedHashMap = new LinkedHashMap<>();
linkedHashMap.put("First", 1);
linkedHashMap.put("Second", 2);
linkedHashMap.put("Third", 3);

// TreeMap (sorted by keys)
Map<String, Integer> treeMap = new TreeMap<>();
treeMap.put("C", 3);
treeMap.put("A", 1);
treeMap.put("B", 2);

// Iterating over maps
// Using keySet
for (String key : hashMap.keySet()) {
    System.out.println(key + ": " + hashMap.get(key));
}

// Using entrySet (more efficient)
for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : hashMap.entrySet()) {
    System.out.println(entry.getKey() + ": " + entry.getValue());
}

// Using forEach (Java 8+)
hashMap.forEach((key, value) -> System.out.println(key + ": " + value));

// Default methods (Java 8+)
hashMap.putIfAbsent("Grape", 40); // Only put if key doesn't exist
hashMap.replace("Apple", 10, 15); // Replace if key and value match
hashMap.computeIfAbsent("Pear", k -> k.length()); // Compute if absent
hashMap.computeIfPresent("Apple", (k, v) -> v * 2); // Compute if present
hashMap.merge("Apple", 5, (oldValue, newValue) -> oldValue + newValue); // Merge values

Queue ​

java
import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.PriorityQueue;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.Queue;

// LinkedList as Queue
Queue<String> queue = new LinkedList<>();
queue.offer("First"); // Add to queue
queue.offer("Second");
queue.offer("Third");
String head = queue.peek(); // Look at head without removing
String removed = queue.poll(); // Remove and return head
int size = queue.size(); // 2

// PriorityQueue (sorted)
Queue<Integer> priorityQueue = new PriorityQueue<>();
priorityQueue.offer(30);
priorityQueue.offer(10);
priorityQueue.offer(20);
int smallest = priorityQueue.peek(); // 10 (smallest element)

// ArrayDeque (more efficient than LinkedList for stack/queue)
Queue<String> arrayDeque = new ArrayDeque<>();
arrayDeque.offer("First");
arrayDeque.offer("Second");
arrayDeque.offer("Third");

// Using as Stack
Deque<String> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
stack.push("First"); // Push to top
stack.push("Second");
String top = stack.peek(); // Look at top
String popped = stack.pop(); // Remove and return top

Object-Oriented Programming ​

Classes and Objects ​

java
public class Person {
    // Fields (instance variables)
    private String name;
    private int age;
    
    // Static field (class variable)
    private static int count = 0;
    
    // Constructor
    public Person(String name, int age) {
        this.name = name;
        this.age = age;
        count++; // Increment static count
    }
    
    // Instance methods
    public String getName() {
        return name;
    }
    
    public void setName(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }
    
    public int getAge() {
        return age;
    }
    
    public void setAge(int age) {
        this.age = age;
    }
    
    public void introduce() {
        System.out.println("Hi, I'm " + name + " and I'm " + age + " years old.");
    }
    
    // Static method
    public static int getCount() {
        return count;
    }
    
    // Overriding toString() method
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "Person{name='" + name + "', age=" + age + "}";
    }
    
    // Overriding equals() and hashCode() methods
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object obj) {
        if (this == obj) return true;
        if (obj == null || getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;
        Person person = (Person) obj;
        return age == person.age && Objects.equals(name, person.name);
    }
    
    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(name, age);
    }
}

// Using the class
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Person person1 = new Person("John", 30);
        Person person2 = new Person("Jane", 25);
        
        person1.introduce();
        person2.introduce();
        
        System.out.println("Total persons: " + Person.getCount());
    }
}

Inheritance ​

java
// Base class (superclass)
public class Animal {
    protected String name;
    
    public Animal(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }
    
    public void eat() {
        System.out.println(name + " is eating.");
    }
    
    public void sleep() {
        System.out.println(name + " is sleeping.");
    }
    
    public void makeSound() {
        System.out.println(name + " makes a sound.");
    }
}

// Derived class (subclass)
public class Dog extends Animal {
    private String breed;
    
    public Dog(String name, String breed) {
        super(name); // Call superclass constructor
        this.breed = breed;
    }
    
    // Override method from superclass
    @Override
    public void makeSound() {
        System.out.println(name + " barks.");
    }
    
    // New method specific to Dog
    public void wagTail() {
        System.out.println(name + " wags tail.");
    }
    
    // Getters and setters
    public String getBreed() {
        return breed;
    }
    
    public void setBreed(String breed) {
        this.breed = breed;
    }
}

// Using inheritance
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Dog dog = new Dog("Buddy", "Golden Retriever");
        dog.eat(); // Inherited method
        dog.sleep(); // Inherited method
        dog.makeSound(); // Overridden method
        dog.wagTail(); // Specific to Dog
    }
}

Polymorphism ​

java
// Base class
abstract class Shape {
    protected String color;
    
    public Shape(String color) {
        this.color = color;
    }
    
    // Abstract method (must be implemented by subclasses)
    public abstract double getArea();
    
    // Concrete method
    public void display() {
        System.out.println("This is a " + color + " shape with area " + getArea());
    }
}

// Subclass
class Circle extends Shape {
    private double radius;
    
    public Circle(String color, double radius) {
        super(color);
        this.radius = radius;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double getArea() {
        return Math.PI * radius * radius;
    }
}

// Another subclass
class Rectangle extends Shape {
    private double width;
    private double height;
    
    public Rectangle(String color, double width, double height) {
        super(color);
        this.width = width;
        this.height = height;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double getArea() {
        return width * height;
    }
}

// Using polymorphism
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Shape[] shapes = {
            new Circle("red", 5.0),
            new Rectangle("blue", 4.0, 6.0),
            new Circle("green", 3.0)
        };
        
        for (Shape shape : shapes) {
            shape.display(); // Polymorphic call
        }
        
        // Using instanceof
        for (Shape shape : shapes) {
            if (shape instanceof Circle) {
                Circle circle = (Circle) shape;
                System.out.println("Circle with radius: " + circle.radius);
            } else if (shape instanceof Rectangle) {
                Rectangle rectangle = (Rectangle) shape;
                System.out.println("Rectangle with dimensions: " + rectangle.width + "x" + rectangle.height);
            }
        }
    }
}

Encapsulation ​

java
public class BankAccount {
    // Private fields (encapsulated)
    private String accountNumber;
    private String accountHolder;
    private double balance;
    
    // Constructor
    public BankAccount(String accountNumber, String accountHolder, double initialBalance) {
        this.accountNumber = accountNumber;
        this.accountHolder = accountHolder;
        this.balance = initialBalance;
    }
    
    // Public getters and setters (controlled access)
    public String getAccountNumber() {
        return accountNumber;
    }
    
    public String getAccountHolder() {
        return accountHolder;
    }
    
    public void setAccountHolder(String accountHolder) {
        this.accountHolder = accountHolder;
    }
    
    public double getBalance() {
        return balance;
    }
    
    // No setter for balance to prevent direct manipulation
    
    // Public methods to interact with the private fields
    public void deposit(double amount) {
        if (amount > 0) {
            balance += amount;
            System.out.println("Deposited: $" + amount + ". New balance: $" + balance);
        } else {
            System.out.println("Invalid deposit amount.");
        }
    }
    
    public boolean withdraw(double amount) {
        if (amount > 0 && amount <= balance) {
            balance -= amount;
            System.out.println("Withdrew: $" + amount + ". New balance: $" + balance);
            return true;
        } else {
            System.out.println("Invalid withdrawal amount or insufficient funds.");
            return false;
        }
    }
    
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "BankAccount{" +
               "accountNumber='" + accountNumber + '\'' +
               ", accountHolder='" + accountHolder + '\'' +
               ", balance=" + balance +
               '}';
    }
}

// Using encapsulation
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        BankAccount account = new BankAccount("123456789", "John Doe", 1000.0);
        
        // Access through public methods
        System.out.println(account);
        account.deposit(500.0);
        account.withdraw(200.0);
        
        // Can't directly access private fields
        // account.balance = 5000.0; // Compile error
    }
}

Abstraction ​

java
// Abstract class
abstract class Vehicle {
    protected String brand;
    protected int year;
    
    public Vehicle(String brand, int year) {
        this.brand = brand;
        this.year = year;
    }
    
    // Concrete method
    public void start() {
        System.out.println("Starting the " + year + " " + brand);
    }
    
    // Abstract methods (must be implemented by subclasses)
    public abstract void accelerate();
    public abstract void brake();
    
    // Template method (defines algorithm skeleton)
    public final void drive() {
        start();
        accelerate();
        System.out.println("Driving...");
        brake();
    }
}

// Concrete subclass
class Car extends Vehicle {
    private int numDoors;
    
    public Car(String brand, int year, int numDoors) {
        super(brand, year);
        this.numDoors = numDoors;
    }
    
    @Override
    public void accelerate() {
        System.out.println("Car is accelerating");
    }
    
    @Override
    public void brake() {
        System.out.println("Car is braking");
    }
    
    public void openTrunk() {
        System.out.println("Opening car trunk");
    }
}

// Another concrete subclass
class Motorcycle extends Vehicle {
    private boolean hasSidecar;
    
    public Motorcycle(String brand, int year, boolean hasSidecar) {
        super(brand, year);
        this.hasSidecar = hasSidecar;
    }
    
    @Override
    public void accelerate() {
        System.out.println("Motorcycle is accelerating");
    }
    
    @Override
    public void brake() {
        System.out.println("Motorcycle is braking");
    }
    
    public void doWheelie() {
        System.out.println("Motorcycle is doing a wheelie");
    }
}

// Using abstraction
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Vehicle car = new Car("Toyota", 2022, 4);
        Vehicle motorcycle = new Motorcycle("Harley-Davidson", 2021, false);
        
        car.drive();
        System.out.println();
        motorcycle.drive();
        
        // Can't call specific methods on Vehicle reference
        // car.openTrunk(); // Compile error
        
        // Need to cast to specific type
        if (car instanceof Car) {
            ((Car) car).openTrunk();
        }
    }
}

Interfaces ​

java
// Interface definition
public interface Drawable {
    // Constant (public, static, final by default)
    double PI = 3.14159;
    
    // Abstract method (public, abstract by default)
    void draw();
    
    // Default method (Java 8+)
    default void resize(double factor) {
        System.out.println("Resizing by factor: " + factor);
    }
    
    // Static method (Java 8+)
    static void printInfo() {
        System.out.println("This is a Drawable interface");
    }
}

// Another interface
public interface Colorable {
    void setColor(String color);
    String getColor();
}

// Class implementing multiple interfaces
public class Circle implements Drawable, Colorable {
    private double radius;
    private String color;
    
    public Circle(double radius, String color) {
        this.radius = radius;
        this.color = color;
    }
    
    @Override
    public void draw() {
        System.out.println("Drawing a " + color + " circle with radius " + radius);
    }
    
    @Override
    public void setColor(String color) {
        this.color = color;
    }
    
    @Override
    public String getColor() {
        return color;
    }
    
    // Override default method
    @Override
    public void resize(double factor) {
        radius *= factor;
        System.out.println("Circle resized. New radius: " + radius);
    }
}

// Using interfaces
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Circle circle = new Circle(5.0, "red");
        
        // As a Circle
        circle.draw();
        circle.resize(1.5);
        
        // As a Drawable
        Drawable drawable = circle;
        drawable.draw();
        drawable.resize(0.8);
        
        // As a Colorable
        Colorable colorable = circle;
        colorable.setColor("blue");
        System.out.println("New color: " + colorable.getColor());
        
        // Static method
        Drawable.printInfo();
    }
}

// Functional interface (has exactly one abstract method)
@FunctionalInterface
interface Calculator {
    double calculate(double a, double b);
    
    // Can have default methods
    default void printResult(double a, double b) {
        System.out.println("Result: " + calculate(a, b));
    }
}

// Using functional interface with lambda
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Addition
        Calculator addition = (a, b) -> a + b;
        addition.printResult(5, 3); // Result: 8.0
        
        // Multiplication
        Calculator multiplication = (a, b) -> a * b;
        multiplication.printResult(5, 3); // Result: 15.0
    }
}

Exception Handling ​

java
// Exception hierarchy
// Throwable
// ├── Error (serious problems, shouldn't be caught)
// └── Exception
//     ├── RuntimeException (unchecked exceptions)
//     └── Other exceptions (checked exceptions)

public class ExceptionExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Try-catch block
        try {
            int result = 10 / 0; // ArithmeticException
        } catch (ArithmeticException e) {
            System.out.println("Caught arithmetic exception: " + e.getMessage());
        }
        
        // Multiple catch blocks
        try {
            String str = null;
            System.out.println(str.length()); // NullPointerException
        } catch (NullPointerException e) {
            System.out.println("Caught null pointer exception");
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.out.println("Caught general exception");
        }
        
        // Finally block (always executed)
        try {
            // Code that might throw an exception
            int[] array = new int[5];
            System.out.println(array[10]); // ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
        } catch (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e) {
            System.out.println("Caught array index out of bounds exception");
        } finally {
            System.out.println("Finally block always executes");
        }
        
        // Try-with-resources (Java 7+)
        try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader("file.txt"))) {
            String line = reader.readLine();
            System.out.println(line);
        } catch (IOException e) {
            System.out.println("Caught IO exception: " + e.getMessage());
        } // reader is automatically closed
        
        // Throwing exceptions
        try {
            validateAge(15);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            System.out.println(e.getMessage());
        }
        
        // Custom exception
        try {
            withdraw(100.0, 150.0);
        } catch (InsufficientFundsException e) {
            System.out.println(e.getMessage());
        }
    }
    
    // Method that throws a checked exception
    public static void validateAge(int age) throws IllegalArgumentException {
        if (age < 18) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Age must be at least 18");
        }
    }
    
    // Method that throws a custom exception
    public static void withdraw(double balance, double amount) throws InsufficientFundsException {
        if (amount > balance) {
            throw new InsufficientFundsException("Insufficient funds. Balance: " + balance + ", Amount: " + amount);
        }
        // Withdraw logic here
    }
}

// Custom exception class
class InsufficientFundsException extends Exception {
    public InsufficientFundsException(String message) {
        super(message);
    }
}

// Chained exceptions
public class ChainedExceptionExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        try {
            method1();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.out.println("Caught exception: " + e.getMessage());
            System.out.println("Caused by: " + e.getCause().getMessage());
        }
    }
    
    public static void method1() throws Exception {
        try {
            method2();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new Exception("Exception in method1", e);
        }
    }
    
    public static void method2() throws Exception {
        throw new Exception("Exception in method2");
    }
}

// Generic class
public class Box<T> {

// Generic method
public class Util {
    // Generic method
    public static <T> void swap(T[] array, int i, int j) {
        T temp = array[i];
        array[i] = array[j];
        array[j] = temp;
    }
    
    // Generic method with bounded type parameter
    public static <T extends Comparable<T>> T max(T x, T y, T z) {
        T max = x;
        if (y.compareTo(max) > 0) {
            max = y;
        }
        if (z.compareTo(max) > 0) {
            max = z;
        }
        return max;
    }
}

// Using generic methods
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Integer[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
        Util.swap(numbers, 0, 4);
        
        String maxString = Util.max("Apple", "Orange", "Banana");
        System.out.println("Maximum: " + maxString); // Orange
    }
}

// Generic interface
public interface Comparable<T> {
    int compareTo(T other);
}

// Wildcards
public class WildcardExample {
    // Upper bounded wildcard
    public static double sumOfList(List<? extends Number> list) {
        double sum = 0.0;
        for (Number n : list) {
            sum += n.doubleValue();
        }
        return sum;
    }
    
    // Lower bounded wildcard
    public static void addNumbers(List<? super Integer> list) {
        for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
            list.add(i);
        }
    }
    
    // Unbounded wildcard
    public static void printList(List<?> list) {
        for (Object elem : list) {
            System.out.print(elem + " ");
        }
        System.out.println();
    }
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Integer> intList = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
        List<Double> doubleList = Arrays.asList(1.1, 2.2, 3.3);
        
        System.out.println("Sum of intList: " + sumOfList(intList));
        System.out.println("Sum of doubleList: " + sumOfList(doubleList));
        
        List<Number> numList = new ArrayList<>();
        addNumbers(numList);
        System.out.println("numList: " + numList);
        
        printList(intList);
        printList(doubleList);
    }
}

Lambda Expressions and Functional Programming ​

java
// Functional interfaces from java.util.function
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.function.Consumer;
import java.util.function.Supplier;
import java.util.function.Function;
import java.util.function.UnaryOperator;
import java.util.function.BinaryOperator;

public class FunctionalInterfaces {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Predicate<T> - boolean test(T t)
        Predicate<Integer> isEven = n -> n % 2 == 0;
        System.out.println(isEven.test(4)); // true
        System.out.println(isEven.test(5)); // false
        
        // Consumer<T> - void accept(T t)
        Consumer<String> printer = str -> System.out.println(str);
        printer.accept("Hello Lambda");
        
        // Supplier<T> - T get()
        Supplier<Double> randomSupplier = () -> Math.random();
        System.out.println(randomSupplier.get());
        
        // Function<T, R> - R apply(T t)
        Function<String, Integer> stringLength = str -> str.length();
        System.out.println(stringLength.apply("Lambda"));
        
        // UnaryOperator<T> - T apply(T t)
        UnaryOperator<String> toUpperCase = str -> str.toUpperCase();
        System.out.println(toUpperCase.apply("hello"));
        
        // BinaryOperator<T> - T apply(T t1, T t2)
        BinaryOperator<Integer> add = (a, b) -> a + b;
        System.out.println(add.apply(5, 3));
    }
}

// Custom functional interface
@FunctionalInterface
interface StringOperation {
    String operate(String str);
    
    // Can have default methods
    default void print(String str) {
        System.out.println(operate(str));
    }
}

public class LambdaExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Lambda expressions
        StringOperation reverse = str -> new StringBuilder(str).reverse().toString();
        StringOperation toUpperCase = str -> str.toUpperCase();
        StringOperation addPrefix = str -> "Prefix: " + str;
        
        reverse.print("Hello"); // olleH
        toUpperCase.print("Hello"); // HELLO
        addPrefix.print("Hello"); // Prefix: Hello
        
        // Method references
        // Static method reference
        Function<String, Integer> parseInt = Integer::parseInt;
        int number = parseInt.apply("123");
        
        // Instance method reference
        String str = "Hello";
        Supplier<Integer> length = str::length;
        
        // Constructor reference
        Supplier<String> stringSupplier = String::new;
        String emptyString = stringSupplier.get();
    }
}

// Using lambdas with collections
public class CollectionLambdas {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> names = Arrays.asList("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David");
        
        // Iterating with forEach
        names.forEach(name -> System.out.println(name));
        
        // Filtering with removeIf
        names.removeIf(name -> name.startsWith("A"));
        
        // Sorting with Comparator
        names.sort((a, b) -> a.compareTo(b));
        
        // Using method reference for sorting
        names.sort(String::compareTo);
        
        // Using lambda with Map
        Map<String, Integer> nameLengths = new HashMap<>();
        names.forEach(name -> nameLengths.put(name, name.length()));
        
        // Using replaceAll with lambda
        nameLengths.replaceAll((name, length) -> length * 2);
    }
}

Streams API ​

java
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

public class StreamExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> names = Arrays.asList("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "Eve");
        
        // Creating streams
        Stream<String> stream1 = names.stream(); // From collection
        Stream<String> stream2 = Arrays.stream(new String[]{"A", "B", "C"}); // From array
        Stream<String> stream3 = Stream.of("A", "B", "C"); // Direct creation
        Stream<String> stream4 = Stream.generate(() -> "Element").limit(5); // Generated stream
        Stream<Integer> stream5 = Stream.iterate(0, n -> n + 2).limit(5); // Iterated stream
        
        // Filtering
        List<String> filteredNames = names.stream()
            .filter(name -> name.length() > 4)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Mapping
        List<Integer> nameLengths = names.stream()
            .map(String::length)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Flat mapping
        List<List<Integer>> nestedLists = Arrays.asList(
            Arrays.asList(1, 2),
            Arrays.asList(3, 4),
            Arrays.asList(5, 6)
        );
        
        List<Integer> flattenedList = nestedLists.stream()
            .flatMap(List::stream)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Distinct
        List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5);
        List<Integer> distinctNumbers = numbers.stream()
            .distinct()
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Sorting
        List<String> sortedNames = names.stream()
            .sorted()
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Custom sorting
        List<String> reverseSortedNames = names.stream()
            .sorted((a, b) -> b.compareTo(a))
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Limit and skip
        List<String> limitedNames = names.stream()
            .skip(1)
            .limit(3)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        // Terminal operations
        // forEach
        names.stream().forEach(System.out::println);
        
        // count
        long count = names.stream().count();
        
        // min and max
        Optional<String> minName = names.stream().min(String::compareTo);
        Optional<String> maxName = names.stream().max(String::compareTo);
        
        // findFirst and findAny
        Optional<String> firstName = names.stream().findFirst();
        Optional<String> anyName = names.stream().findAny();
        
        // anyMatch, allMatch, noneMatch
        boolean anyMatch = names.stream().anyMatch(name -> name.startsWith("A"));
        boolean allMatch = names.stream().allMatch(name -> name.length() > 2);
        boolean noneMatch = names.stream().noneMatch(name -> name.length() > 10);
        
        // Reduction
        Optional<String> reducedName = names.stream()
            .reduce((a, b) -> a + ", " + b);
        
        int sum = numbers.stream()
            .reduce(0, Integer::sum);
        
        // Collecting results
        List<String> collectedList = names.stream()
            .filter(name -> name.length() > 4)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        
        Set<String> collectedSet = names.stream()
            .filter(name -> name.length() > 4)
            .collect(Collectors.toSet());
        
        Map<String, Integer> collectedMap = names.stream()
            .collect(Collectors.toMap(name -> name, String::length));
        
        // Grouping
        Map<Integer, List<String>> namesByLength = names.stream()
            .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(String::length));
        
        // Partitioning
        Map<Boolean, List<String>> partitionedNames = names.stream()
            .collect(Collectors.partitioningBy(name -> name.length() > 4));
        
        // Joining strings
        String joinedNames = names.stream()
            .collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
        
        // Parallel streams
        List<String> parallelProcessedNames = names.parallelStream()
            .map(String::toUpperCase)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }
}

// Primitive streams

        Stream<Integer> boxedStream = IntStream.range(1, 11).boxed();

import java.util.*;

// List implementations
public class ListExamples {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // ArrayList - dynamic array, fast random access
        List<String> arrayList = new ArrayList<>();
        arrayList.add("Apple");
        arrayList.add("Banana");
        arrayList.add("Orange");
        
        // Access elements
        String first = arrayList.get(0);
        
        // Remove element
        arrayList.remove("Banana");
        
        // Check if contains
        boolean containsApple = arrayList.contains("Apple");
        
        // Size
        int size = arrayList.size();
        
        // Iterate
        for (String fruit : arrayList) {
            System.out.println(fruit);
        }
        
        // LinkedList - doubly-linked list, fast insertion/deletion
        List<Integer> linkedList = new LinkedList<>();
        linkedList.add(1);
        linkedList.add(2);
        linkedList.add(3);
        
        // Add at specific position
        linkedList.add(1, 5); // [1, 5, 2, 3]
        
        // Convert to array
        String[] array = arrayList.toArray(new String[0]);
        
        // Sorting
        Collections.sort(arrayList);
        
        // Custom sorting with Comparator
        arrayList.sort((a, b) -> b.compareTo(a));
        
        // Immutable list (Java 9+)
        List<String> immutableList = List.of("A", "B", "C");
        
        // Unmodifiable view
        List<String> unmodifiableList = Collections.unmodifiableList(arrayList);
    }
}

// Set implementations
public class SetExamples {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // HashSet - no ordering, fast operations
        Set<String> hashSet = new HashSet<>();
        hashSet.add("Apple");
        hashSet.add("Banana");
        hashSet.add("Orange");
        hashSet.add("Apple"); // Duplicate, won't be added
        
        // Check if contains
        boolean containsApple = hashSet.contains("Apple");
        
        // Remove element
        hashSet.remove("Banana");
        
        // TreeSet - sorted set
        Set<Integer> treeSet = new TreeSet<>();
        treeSet.add(5);
        treeSet.add(2);
        treeSet.add(8);
        treeSet.add(1);
        // Automatically sorted: [1, 2, 5, 8]
        
        // LinkedHashSet - insertion order
        Set<String> linkedHashSet = new LinkedHashSet<>();
        linkedHashSet.add("First");
        linkedHashSet.add("Second");
        linkedHashSet.add("Third");
        
        // Immutable set (Java 9+)
        Set<String> immutableSet = Set.of("A", "B", "C");
        
        // Set operations
        Set<Integer> set1 = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4));
        Set<Integer> set2 = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(3, 4, 5, 6));
        
        // Union
        Set<Integer> union = new HashSet<>(set1);
        union.addAll(set2); // [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
        
        // Intersection
        Set<Integer> intersection = new HashSet<>(set1);
        intersection.retainAll(set2); // [3, 4]
        
        // Difference
        Set<Integer> difference = new HashSet<>(set1);
        difference.removeAll(set2); // [1, 2]
    }
}

// Map implementations
public class MapExamples {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // HashMap - no ordering, fast operations
        Map<String, Integer> hashMap = new HashMap<>();
        hashMap.put("Alice", 25);
        hashMap.put("Bob", 30);
        hashMap.put("Charlie", 35);
        
        // Get value
        Integer aliceAge = hashMap.get("Alice");
        
        // Get with default value
        Integer unknownAge = hashMap.getOrDefault("Unknown", 0);
        
        // Check if contains key or value
        boolean hasAlice = hashMap.containsKey("Alice");
        boolean hasAge30 = hashMap.containsValue(30);
        
        // Remove entry
        hashMap.remove("Bob");
        
        // Iterate over keys
        for (String name : hashMap.keySet()) {
            System.out.println(name + ": " + hashMap.get(name));
        }
        
        // Iterate over entries
        for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : hashMap.entrySet()) {
            System.out.println(entry.getKey() + ": " + entry.getValue());
        }
        
        // TreeMap - sorted map
        Map<String, Integer> treeMap = new TreeMap<>();
        treeMap.put("Zebra", 1);
        treeMap.put("Apple", 2);
        treeMap.put("Banana", 3);
        // Automatically sorted by key: {Apple=2, Banana=3, Zebra=1}
        
        // LinkedHashMap - insertion order
        Map<String, Integer> linkedHashMap = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        linkedHashMap.put("First", 1);
        linkedHashMap.put("Second", 2);
        linkedHashMap.put("Third", 3);
        
        // Immutable map (Java 9+)
        Map<String, Integer> immutableMap = Map.of("A", 1, "B", 2, "C", 3);
        
        // Compute if absent
        hashMap.computeIfAbsent("David", k -> 40);
        
        // Compute if present
        hashMap.computeIfPresent("Alice", (k, v) -> v + 1);
        
        // Merge
        hashMap.merge("Alice", 1, Integer::sum);
    }
}

// Queue implementations
public class QueueExamples {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // LinkedList as Queue
        Queue<String> queue = new LinkedList<>();
        queue.offer("First"); // Add to queue
        queue.offer("Second");
        queue.offer("Third");
        
        // Peek at head without removing
        String head = queue.peek(); // "First"
        
        // Remove and return head
        String removed = queue.poll(); // "First"
        
        // PriorityQueue - priority queue
        PriorityQueue<Integer> priorityQueue = new PriorityQueue<>();
        priorityQueue.offer(5);
        priorityQueue.offer(2);
        priorityQueue.offer(8);
        priorityQueue.offer(1);
        
        // Elements are ordered by natural ordering
        Integer smallest = priorityQueue.peek(); // 1
        
        // Deque - double-ended queue
        Deque<String> deque = new ArrayDeque<>();
        deque.addFirst("First");
        deque.addLast("Last");
        
        String first = deque.removeFirst();
        String last = deque.removeLast();
    }
}

// Concurrent collections
public class ConcurrentCollectionsExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // ConcurrentHashMap - thread-safe HashMap
        Map<String, Integer> concurrentMap = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
        concurrentMap.put("Key1", 1);
        concurrentMap.put("Key2", 2);
        
        // ConcurrentLinkedQueue - thread-safe queue
        Queue<String> concurrentQueue = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();
        concurrentQueue.offer("Element1");
        concurrentQueue.offer("Element2");
        
        // CopyOnWriteArrayList - thread-safe list
        List<String> copyOnWriteList = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
        copyOnWriteList.add("Item1");
        copyOnWriteList.add("Item2");
        
        // BlockingQueue
        BlockingQueue<String> blockingQueue = new LinkedBlockingQueue<>();
        try {
            blockingQueue.put("Item"); // Blocks if queue is full
            String item = blockingQueue.take(); // Blocks if queue is empty
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
    }
}

import java.time.*;
import java.time.format.*;
import java.time.temporal.*;

public class DateTimeExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // LocalDate - date without time
        LocalDate today = LocalDate.now();
        LocalDate birthday = LocalDate.of(1990, Month.JANUARY, 15);
        LocalDate parsedDate = LocalDate.parse("2023-12-25");
        
        // LocalTime - time without date
        LocalTime now = LocalTime.now();
        LocalTime specificTime = LocalTime.of(14, 30, 45);
        LocalTime parsedTime = LocalTime.parse("14:30:45");
        
        // LocalDateTime - date and time
        LocalDateTime nowDateTime = LocalDateTime.now();
        LocalDateTime specificDateTime = LocalDateTime.of(2023, 12, 25, 14, 30);
        LocalDateTime parsedDateTime = LocalDateTime.parse("2023-12-25T14:30:45");
        
        // ZonedDateTime - date and time with time zone
        ZoneId zoneId = ZoneId.of("America/New_York");
        ZonedDateTime zonedDateTime = ZonedDateTime.now(zoneId);
        ZonedDateTime parsedZonedDateTime = ZonedDateTime.parse("2023-12-25T14:30:45-05:00[America/New_York]");
        
        // Instant - point on the time-line (UTC)
        Instant nowInstant = Instant.now();
        Instant specificInstant = Instant.parse("2023-12-25T14:30:45Z");
        
        // Duration - amount of time in terms of seconds and nanoseconds
        Duration duration = Duration.between(LocalTime.of(10, 0), LocalTime.of(12, 30));
        long minutes = duration.toMinutes(); // 150
        
        // Period - amount of time in terms of years, months, and days
        Period period = Period.between(LocalDate.of(2020, 1, 1), LocalDate.of(2023, 6, 15));
        int years = period.getYears(); // 3
        int months = period.getMonths(); // 5
        int days = period.getDays(); // 14
        
        // DateTimeFormatter - formatting and parsing
        DateTimeFormatter formatter = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss");
        String formattedDateTime = nowDateTime.format(formatter);
        LocalDateTime parsedFromFormat = LocalDateTime.parse("2023-12-25 14:30:45", formatter);
        
        // ISO format
        String isoDate = today.format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE);
        String isoDateTime = nowDateTime.format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME);
        
        // Manipulating dates and times
        LocalDate tomorrow = today.plusDays(1);
        LocalDate lastMonth = today.minusMonths(1);
        LocalDateTime nextYear = nowDateTime.plusYears(1);
        
        // Adjusting dates
        LocalDate firstDayOfMonth = today.with(TemporalAdjusters.firstDayOfMonth());
        LocalDate lastDayOfMonth = today.with(TemporalAdjusters.lastDayOfMonth());
        LocalDate nextMonday = today.with(TemporalAdjusters.next(DayOfWeek.MONDAY));
        
        // Getting parts of dates and times
        int year = today.getYear();
        Month month = today.getMonth();
        int day = today.getDayOfMonth();
        DayOfWeek dayOfWeek = today.getDayOfWeek();
        int hour = nowDateTime.getHour();
        int minute = nowDateTime.getMinute();
        
        // Comparing dates and times
        boolean isBefore = today.isBefore(birthday);
        boolean isAfter = today.isAfter(birthday);
        boolean isEqual = today.isEqual(parsedDate);
        
        // Converting between types
        ZonedDateTime utcDateTime = nowInstant.atZone(ZoneId.of("UTC"));
        Instant fromDateTime = nowDateTime.toInstant(ZoneOffset.UTC);
        LocalDate fromDateTime2 = nowDateTime.toLocalDate();
        LocalTime fromDateTime3 = nowDateTime.toLocalTime();
        
        // Working with time zones
        ZoneId systemZone = ZoneId.systemDefault();
        Set<String> availableZoneIds = ZoneId.getAvailableZoneIds();
        
        // Converting between time zones
        ZonedDateTime newYorkTime = ZonedDateTime.now(ZoneId.of("America/New_York"));
        ZonedDateTime londonTime = newYorkTime.withZoneSameInstant(ZoneId.of("Europe/London"));
        
        // Working with timestamps
        long epochSeconds = nowInstant.getEpochSecond();
        long epochMillis = nowInstant.toEpochMilli();
        Instant fromEpochSeconds = Instant.ofEpochSecond(epochSeconds);
        Instant fromEpochMillis = Instant.ofEpochMilli(epochMillis);
    }
}

import java.io.*;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.nio.charset.*;
import java.util.*;

public class IOExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        // Working with files using java.nio.file (Java 7+)
        Path path = Paths.get("example.txt");
        
        // Check if file exists
        boolean exists = Files.exists(path);
        
        // Create file
        if (!Files.exists(path)) {
            Files.createFile(path);
        }
        
        // Write to file
        List<String> lines = Arrays.asList("Line 1", "Line 2", "Line 3");
        Files.write(path, lines, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
        
        // Read from file
        List<String> readLines = Files.readAllLines(path);
        
        // Read all content as string
        String content = new String(Files.readAllBytes(path), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        
        // Append to file
        Files.write(path, "New line\n".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
        
        // Copy file
        Path copiedPath = Paths.get("example_copy.txt");
        Files.copy(path, copiedPath, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        
        // Move file
        Path movedPath = Paths.get("example_moved.txt");
        Files.move(path, movedPath, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        
        // Delete file
        Files.deleteIfExists(movedPath);
        
        // Working with directories
        Path dirPath = Paths.get("example_dir");
        if (!Files.exists(dirPath)) {
            Files.createDirectory(dirPath);
        }
        
        // Create directories
        Path nestedDirPath = Paths.get("example_dir/nested");
        Files.createDirectories(nestedDirPath);
        
        // List directory contents
        try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream = Files.newDirectoryStream(dirPath)) {
            for (Path entry : stream) {
                System.out.println(entry.getFileName());
            }
        }
        
        // List directory with glob pattern
        try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream = Files.newDirectoryStream(dirPath, "*.txt")) {
            for (Path entry : stream) {
                System.out.println(entry.getFileName());
            }
        }
        
        // File attributes
        boolean isRegularFile = Files.isRegularFile(path);
        boolean isDirectory = Files.isDirectory(dirPath);
        boolean isReadable = Files.isReadable(path);
        boolean isWritable = Files.isWritable(path);
        boolean isExecutable = Files.isExecutable(path);
        long size = Files.size(path);
        
        // File permissions
        Set<PosixFilePermission> permissions = Files.getPosixFilePermissions(path);
        permissions.add(PosixFilePermission.OWNER_EXECUTE);
        Files.setPosixFilePermissions(path, permissions);
        
        // Traditional I/O with streams
        // Reading with BufferedReader
        try (BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(path, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            String line;
            while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
                System.out.println(line);
            }
        }
        
        // Writing with BufferedWriter
        try (BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(path, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            writer.write("Line 1\n");
            writer.write("Line 2\n");
            writer.write("Line 3\n");
        }
        
        // Reading with FileReader
        try (FileReader fileReader = new FileReader(path.toFile());
             BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(fileReader)) {
            String line;
            while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
                System.out.println(line);
            }
        }
        
        // Writing with FileWriter
        try (FileWriter fileWriter = new FileWriter(path.toFile());
             BufferedWriter writer = new BufferedWriter(fileWriter)) {
            writer.write("Line 1\n");
            writer.write("Line 2\n");
            writer.write("Line 3\n");
        }
        
        // Binary I/O
        Path binaryPath = Paths.get("binary.dat");
        try (DataOutputStream dos = new DataOutputStream(
                new BufferedOutputStream(Files.newOutputStream(binaryPath)))) {
            dos.writeInt(42);
            dos.writeDouble(3.14159);
            dos.writeUTF("Hello, World!");
        }
        
        try (DataInputStream dis = new DataInputStream(
                new BufferedInputStream(Files.newInputStream(binaryPath)))) {
            int intValue = dis.readInt();
            double doubleValue = dis.readDouble();
            String stringValue = dis.readUTF();
            
            System.out.println("Int: " + intValue);
            System.out.println("Double: " + doubleValue);
            System.out.println("String: " + stringValue);
        }
        
        // Serialization
        Person person = new Person("John Doe", 30);
        Path serializedPath = Paths.get("person.ser");
        
        // Serialize object
        try (ObjectOutputStream oos = new ObjectOutputStream(
                Files.newOutputStream(serializedPath))) {
            oos.writeObject(person);
        }
        
        // Deserialize object
        try (ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(
                Files.newInputStream(serializedPath))) {
            Person deserializedPerson = (Person) ois.readObject();
            System.out.println("Name: " + deserializedPerson.getName());
            System.out.println("Age: " + deserializedPerson.getAge());
        } catch (ClassNotFoundException e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        }
        
        // Working with temporary files
        Path tempFile = Files.createTempFile("prefix", ".suffix");
        try {
            Files.write(tempFile, "Temporary content".getBytes());
            // Use temp file
        } finally {
            Files.deleteIfExists(tempFile);
        }
        
        // Working with temporary directories
        Path tempDir = Files.createTempDirectory("tempDir");
        try {
            // Use temp directory
        } finally {
            // Clean up
            try (DirectoryStream<Path> stream = Files.newDirectoryStream(tempDir)) {
                for (Path entry : stream) {
                    Files.deleteIfExists(entry);
                }
            }
            Files.deleteIfExists(tempDir);
        }
    }
}

Concurrency ​

java
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.*;
import java.util.concurrent.locks.*;
import java.util.*;

// Creating and managing threads
public class ThreadExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        // Creating a thread with Runnable
        Runnable task = () -> {
            for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
                System.out.println("Thread: " + i);
                try {
                    Thread.sleep(100);
                } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                }
            }
        };
        
        Thread thread1 = new Thread(task);
        thread1.start();
        
        // Creating a thread by extending Thread class
        Thread thread2 = new Thread() {
            @Override
            public void run() {
                for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
                    System.out.println("Extended Thread: " + i);
                    try {
                        Thread.sleep(100);
                    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                    }
                }
            }
        };
        thread2.start();
        
        // Wait for threads to complete
        thread1.join();
        thread2.join();
        
        // Thread properties
        System.out.println("Main thread name: " + Thread.currentThread().getName());
        System.out.println("Main thread priority: " + Thread.currentThread().getPriority());
        System.out.println("Main thread state: " + Thread.currentThread().getState());
        
        // Daemon threads
        Thread daemonThread = new Thread(() -> {
            while (true) {
                try {
                    System.out.println("Daemon thread running");
                    Thread.sleep(1000);
                } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                    break;
                }
            }
        });
        daemonThread.setDaemon(true);
        daemonThread.start();
        
        // Main thread sleeps for a short time
        Thread.sleep(3000);
        System.out.println("Main thread ending, daemon thread will terminate");
    }
}

// Synchronization
public class SynchronizationExample {
    private static int counter = 0;
    private static final Object lock = new Object();
    
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        // Using synchronized method
        class Counter {
            private int count = 0;
            
            public synchronized void increment() {
                count++;
            }
            
            public synchronized int getCount() {
                return count;
            }
        }
        
        Counter counter = new Counter();
        
        Thread[] threads = new Thread[10];
        for (int i = 0; i < threads.length; i++) {
            threads[i] = new Thread(() -> {
                for (int j = 0; j < 1000; j++) {
                    counter.increment();
                }
            });
            threads[i].start();
        }
        
        for (Thread thread : threads) {
            thread.join();
        }
        
        System.out.println("Counter value: " + counter.getCount()); // Should be 10000
        
        // Using synchronized block
        for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
            new Thread(() -> {
                for (int j = 0; j < 1000; j++) {
                    synchronized (lock) {
                        SynchronizationExample.counter++;
                    }
                }
            }).start();
        }
        
        Thread.sleep(2000);
        System.out.println("Static counter value: " + SynchronizationExample.counter);
    }
}

// Using locks
public class LockExample {
    private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private int count = 0;
    
    public void increment() {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            count++;
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }
    
    public int getCount() {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            return count;
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }
    
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        LockExample example = new LockExample();
        
        Thread[] threads = new Thread[10];
        for (int i = 0; i < threads.length; i++) {
            threads[i] = new Thread(() -> {
                for (int j = 0; j < 1000; j++) {
                    example.increment();
                }
            });
            threads[i].start();
        }
        
        for (Thread thread : threads) {
            thread.join();
        }
        
        System.out.println("Count: " + example.getCount());
    }
}

// Using ReadWriteLock
public class ReadWriteLockExample {
    private final ReadWriteLock rwLock = new ReentrantReadWriteLock();
    private final Lock readLock = rwLock.readLock();
    private final Lock writeLock = rwLock.writeLock();
    private final List<String> data = new ArrayList<>();
    
    public void add(String item) {
        writeLock.lock();
        try {
            data.add(item);
        } finally {
            writeLock.unlock();
        }
    }
    
    public String get(int index) {
        readLock.lock();
        try {
            return data.get(index);
        } finally {
            readLock.unlock();
        }
    }
    
    public int size() {
        readLock.lock();
        try {
            return data.size();
        } finally {
            readLock.unlock();
        }
    }
}

// Using atomic variables
public class AtomicExample {
    private static AtomicInteger atomicInt = new AtomicInteger(0);
    private static AtomicLong atomicLong = new AtomicLong(0);
    private static AtomicBoolean atomicBoolean = new AtomicBoolean(false);
    private static AtomicReference<String> atomicRef = new AtomicReference<>("Initial");
    
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        Thread[] threads = new Thread[10];
        for (int i = 0; i < threads.length; i++) {
            threads[i] = new Thread(() -> {
                for (int j = 0; j < 1000; j++) {
                    atomicInt.incrementAndGet();
                    atomicLong.incrementAndGet();
                    atomicBoolean.set(true);
                    atomicRef.compareAndSet("Initial", "Updated");
                }
            });
            threads[i].start();
        }
        
        for (Thread thread : threads) {
            thread.join();
        }
        
        System.out.println("Atomic int: " + atomicInt.get());
        System.out.println("Atomic long: " + atomicLong.get());
        System.out.println("Atomic boolean: " + atomicBoolean.get());
        System.out.println("Atomic reference: " + atomicRef.get());
    }
}

// Thread pools
public class ThreadPoolExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Fixed thread pool
        ExecutorService fixedThreadPool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(5);
        
        for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
            final int taskId = i;
            fixedThreadPool.submit(() -> {
                System.out.println("Task " + taskId + " executed by " + Thread.currentThread().getName());
                try {
                    Thread.sleep(1000);
                } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                }
            });
        }
        
        // Cached thread pool
        ExecutorService cachedThreadPool = Executors.newCachedThreadPool();
        
        // Single thread executor
        ExecutorService singleThreadExecutor = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor();
        
        // Scheduled thread pool
        ScheduledExecutorService scheduledThreadPool = Executors.newScheduledThreadPool(3);
        
        // Schedule a task to run after a delay
        scheduledThreadPool.schedule(() -> {
            System.out.println("Delayed task executed");
        }, 5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        
        // Schedule a task to run periodically
        scheduledThreadPool.scheduleAtFixedRate(() -> {
            System.out.println("Periodic task executed at " + System.currentTimeMillis());
        }, 1, 3, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        
        // Shutdown thread pools
        fixedThreadPool.shutdown();
        cachedThreadPool.shutdown();
        singleThreadExecutor.shutdown();
        
        try {
            // Wait for tasks to complete
            if (!fixedThreadPool.awaitTermination(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
                fixedThreadPool.shutdownNow();
            }
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            fixedThreadPool.shutdownNow();
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        }
        
        // Don't shutdown scheduledThreadPool here to allow periodic task to run
    }
}

// Callable and Future
public class CallableFutureExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws ExecutionException, InterruptedException {
        ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);
        
        // Submit a Callable task
        Future<Integer> future1 = executor.submit(() -> {
            Thread.sleep(1000);
            return 42;
        });
        
        Future<String> future2 = executor.submit(() -> {
            Thread.sleep(2000);
            return "Hello, World!";
        });
        
        // Get results (blocking)
        Integer result1 = future1.get();
        String result2 = future2.get();
        
        System.out.println("Result 1: " + result1);
        System.out.println("Result 2: " + result2);
        
        // Submit multiple tasks and get results
        List<Callable<String>> tasks = Arrays.asList(
            () -> "Task 1",
            () -> "Task 2",
            () -> "Task 3"
        );
        
        List<Future<String>> futures = executor.invokeAll(tasks);
        
        for (Future<String> future : futures) {
            System.out.println(future.get());
        }
        
        executor.shutdown();
    }
}

// CompletableFuture (Java 8+)
public class CompletableFutureExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws ExecutionException, InterruptedException {
        // Create a CompletableFuture
        CompletableFuture<String> future = new CompletableFuture<>();
        
        // Complete it manually (in a real scenario, this might be done by another thread)
        new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                Thread.sleep(1000);
                future.complete("Hello from CompletableFuture");
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                future.completeExceptionally(e);
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            }
        }).start();
        
        // Process the result
        future.thenAccept(result -> System.out.println("Result: " + result));
        
        // Supply async
        CompletableFuture<String> supplyFuture = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> {
            try {
                Thread.sleep(1000);
                return "Hello from supplyAsync";
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                return "Error";
            }
        });
        
        // Chain operations
        CompletableFuture<String> chainedFuture = supplyFuture
            .thenApply(result -> result.toUpperCase())
            .thenApply(result -> "Processed: " + result);
        
        System.out.println(chainedFuture.get());
        
        // Combine futures
        CompletableFuture<String> future1 = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> "Hello");
        CompletableFuture<String> future2 = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> "World");
        
        CompletableFuture<String> combinedFuture = future1
            .thenCombine(future2, (s1, s2) -> s1 + ", " + s2);
        
        System.out.println(combinedFuture.get());
        
        // Handle exceptions
        CompletableFuture<String> exceptionalFuture = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> {
            throw new RuntimeException("Something went wrong");
        }).handle((result, ex) -> {
            if (ex != null) {
                return "Error handled: " + ex.getMessage();
            }
            return result;
        });
        
        System.out.println(exceptionalFuture.get());
        
        // Wait for all futures to complete
        CompletableFuture<Void> allFutures = CompletableFuture.allOf(
            CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> "Task 1"),
            CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> "Task 2"),
            CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> "Task 3")
        );
        
        allFutures.get(); // Wait for all to complete
        System.out.println("All tasks completed");
    }
}

java
import java.lang.reflect.*;
import java.util.*;

public class ReflectionExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // Getting Class objects
        Class<?> stringClass = String.class;
        Class<?> stringClass2 = Class.forName("java.lang.String");
        Class<?> stringClass3 = "Hello".getClass();
        
        System.out.println("Class name: " + stringClass.getName());
        System.out.println("Simple name: " + stringClass.getSimpleName());
        System.out.println("Package: " + stringClass.getPackage().getName());
        System.out.println("Superclass: " + stringClass.getSuperclass().getName());
        
        // Getting modifiers
        int modifiers = stringClass.getModifiers();
        System.out.println("Is public: " + Modifier.isPublic(modifiers));
        System.out.println("Is final: " + Modifier.isFinal(modifiers));
        System.out.println("Is interface: " + Modifier.isInterface(modifiers));
        
        // Getting interfaces
        Class<?>[] interfaces = stringClass.getInterfaces();
        for (Class<?> iface : interfaces) {
            System.out.println("Interface: " + iface.getName());
        }
        
        // Getting constructors
        Constructor<?>[] constructors = stringClass.getConstructors();
        for (Constructor<?> constructor : constructors) {
            System.out.println("Constructor: " + constructor);
        }
        
        // Getting specific constructor
        Constructor<String> constructor = String.class.getConstructor(byte[].class);
        byte[] bytes = "Hello".getBytes();
        String str = constructor.newInstance(bytes);
        System.out.println("Created string: " + str);
        
        // Getting fields
        Field[] fields = stringClass.getDeclaredFields();
        for (Field field : fields) {
            System.out.println("Field: " + field.getName() + " of type " + field.getType().getName());
        }
        
        // Getting specific field
        Field valueField = String.class.getDeclaredField("value");
        valueField.setAccessible(true); // Make private field accessible
        
        String testString = "Hello";
        byte[] value = (byte[]) valueField.get(testString);
        System.out.println("Internal value: " + new String(value));
        
        // Getting methods
        Method[] methods = stringClass.getDeclaredMethods();
        for (Method method : methods) {
            System.out.println("Method: " + method.getName() + " with return type " + method.getReturnType().getName());
        }
        
        // Getting specific method
        Method substringMethod = String.class.getMethod("substring", int.class, int.class);
        String result = (String) substringMethod.invoke("Hello World", 6, 11);
        System.out.println("Substring result: " + result);
        
        // Getting all methods from class hierarchy
        Set<Method> allMethods = new HashSet<>();
        Class<?> currentClass = stringClass;
        while (currentClass != null) {
            allMethods.addAll(Arrays.asList(currentClass.getDeclaredMethods()));
            currentClass = currentClass.getSuperclass();
        }
        
        System.out.println("Total methods: " + allMethods.size());
        
        // Creating instances dynamically
        Class<?> arrayListClass = Class.forName("java.util.ArrayList");
        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
        List<String> list = (List<String>) arrayListClass.newInstance();
        list.add("Item 1");
        list.add("Item 2");
        System.out.println("List: " + list);
        
        // Working with arrays
        String[] stringArray = {"A", "B", "C"};
        Class<?> arrayClass = stringArray.getClass();
        System.out.println("Array component type: " + arrayClass.getComponentType().getName());
        System.out.println("Array length: " + Array.getLength(stringArray));
        
        // Modify array element
        Array.set(stringArray, 0, "X");
        System.out.println("Modified array: " + Arrays.toString(stringArray));
        
        // Working with annotations
        Class<MyClass> myClassClass = MyClass.class;
        if (myClassClass.isAnnotationPresent(MyAnnotation.class)) {
            MyAnnotation annotation = myClassClass.getAnnotation(MyAnnotation.class);
            System.out.println("Annotation value: " + annotation.value());
        }
        
        // Getting method annotations
        Method myMethod = myClassClass.getMethod("myMethod");
        if (myMethod.isAnnotationPresent(MyAnnotation.class)) {
            MyAnnotation annotation = myMethod.getAnnotation(MyAnnotation.class);
            System.out.println("Method annotation value: " + annotation.value());
        }
        
        // Getting field annotations
        Field myField = myClassClass.getDeclaredField("myField");
        if (myField.isAnnotationPresent(MyAnnotation.class)) {
            MyAnnotation annotation = myField.getAnnotation(MyAnnotation.class);
            System.out.println("Field annotation value: " + annotation.value());
        }
        
        // Invoking private methods
        Method privateMethod = myClassClass.getDeclaredMethod("privateMethod");
        privateMethod.setAccessible(true);
        privateMethod.invoke(myClassClass.newInstance());
    }
}

Annotations ​

java
import java.lang.annotation.*;
import java.lang.reflect.*;

// Defining annotations
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@Target(ElementType.TYPE)
@interface Author {
    String name();
    String date();
}

@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@Target(ElementType.METHOD)
@interface Version {
    int major();
    int minor();
}

@Retention(RetentionPolicy.SOURCE)
@Target(ElementType.FIELD)
@interface DeprecatedField {
    String reason() default "This field is deprecated";
}

// Using annotations
@Author(name = "John Doe", date = "2023-01-01")
class AnnotatedClass {
    @DeprecatedField(reason = "Use newField instead")
    private String oldField;
    
    private String newField;
    
    @Version(major = 1, minor = 0)
    public void methodV1() {
        System.out.println("Method version 1.0");
    }
    
    @Version(major = 2, minor = 0)
    public void methodV2() {
        System.out.println("Method version 2.0");
    }
}

// Processing annotations at runtime
public class AnnotationProcessor {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Process class annotations
        Class<AnnotatedClass> clazz = AnnotatedClass.class;
        
        if (clazz.isAnnotationPresent(Author.class)) {
            Author author = clazz.getAnnotation(Author.class);
            System.out.println("Class author: " + author.name());
            System.out.println("Class date: " + author.date());
        }
        
        // Process method annotations
        for (Method method : clazz.getDeclaredMethods()) {
            if (method.isAnnotationPresent(Version.class)) {
                Version version = method.getAnnotation(Version.class);
                System.out.println("Method " + method.getName() + 
                                  " version: " + version.major() + "." + version.minor());
            }
        }
        
        // Process field annotations
        for (Field field : clazz.getDeclaredFields()) {
            if (field.isAnnotationPresent(DeprecatedField.class)) {
                DeprecatedField deprecated = field.getAnnotation(DeprecatedField.class);
                System.out.println("Field " + field.getName() + 
                                  " is deprecated: " + deprecated.reason());
            }
        }
    }
}

// Built-in annotations examples
public class BuiltInAnnotations {
    // @Override - indicates method overrides a superclass method
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "BuiltInAnnotations";
    }
    
    // @Deprecated - marks element as deprecated
    @Deprecated
    public void oldMethod() {
        System.out.println("This method is deprecated");
    }
    
    // @SuppressWarnings - suppresses compiler warnings
    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    public void suppressWarningsExample() {
        List list = new ArrayList(); // Raw type, warning suppressed
        list.add("Item");
    }
    
    // @SafeVarargs - indicates a method doesn't perform unsafe operations on varargs
    @SafeVarargs
    public final <T> void safeVarargsMethod(T... items) {
        for (T item : items) {
            System.out.println(item);
        }
    }
    
    // @FunctionalInterface - indicates an interface is a functional interface
    @FunctionalInterface
    interface MyFunctionalInterface {
        void doSomething();
        
        // Can have default methods
        default void defaultMethod() {
            System.out.println("Default method");
        }
        
        // Can have static methods
        static void staticMethod() {
            System.out.println("Static method");
        }
        
        // Can have Object methods
        @Override
        boolean equals(Object obj);
    }
    
    // @Repeatable - indicates annotation can be applied multiple times
    @Repeatable(Authors.class)
    @interface Author {
        String name();
    }
    
    @interface Authors {
        Author[] value();
    }
    
    // Using repeatable annotation
    @Author(name = "Alice")
    @Author(name = "Bob")
    class RepeatableExample {
    }
}
