java
// module-info.java
module com.example.myapp {
    // Dependencies on other modules
    requires java.base; // Implicitly required
    requires java.logging;
    requires java.sql;
    
    // Optional dependencies
    requires static org.slf4j;
    
    // Transitive dependencies (automatically available to consumers)
    requires transitive com.google.gson;
    
    // Exported packages
    exports com.example.myapp.api;
    exports com.example.myapp.util to com.example.otherapp; // Export to specific module
    
    // Open packages for reflection
    opens com.example.myapp.internal to org.hibernate;
    
    // Services provided by this module
    provides com.example.api.Service with com.example.myapp.impl.ServiceImpl;
    
    // Services consumed by this module
    uses com.example.api.Plugin;
}

// Using services
public class ServiceLoaderExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Load all implementations of a service interface
        ServiceLoader<Service> services = ServiceLoader.load(Service.class);
        
        // Use each implementation
        for (Service service : services) {
            service.doSomething();
        }
        
        // Stream API for services (Java 9+)
        ServiceLoader<Service> serviceLoader = ServiceLoader.load(Service.class);
        serviceLoader.stream()
            .filter(provider -> provider.type().getName().contains("Impl"))
            .findFirst()
            .ifPresent(provider -> provider.get().doSomething());
    }
}

// Service interface
public interface Service {
    void doSomething();
}

// Service implementation
public class ServiceImpl implements Service {
    @Override
    public void doSomething() {
        System.out.println("ServiceImpl is doing something");
    }
}

// Module-aware reflection
public class ModuleReflectionExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // Get current module
        Module currentModule = ModuleReflectionExample.class.getModule();
        System.out.println("Current module: " + currentModule.getName());
        
        // Check if module exports a package
        boolean exportsApi = currentModule.isExported("com.example.myapp.api");
        System.out.println("Exports API package: " + exportsApi);
        
        // Check if module opens a package
        boolean opensInternal = currentModule.isOpen("com.example.myapp.internal");
        System.out.println("Opens internal package: " + opensInternal);
        
        // Add exports/opens at runtime
        Module otherModule = Class.forName("com.example.otherapp.OtherClass").getModule();
        currentModule.addExports("com.example.myapp.internal", otherModule);
        currentModule.addOpens("com.example.myapp.internal", otherModule);
        
        // Read module descriptor
        ModuleDescriptor descriptor = currentModule.getDescriptor();
        System.out.println("Requires: " + descriptor.requires());
        System.out.println("Exports: " + descriptor.exports());
        System.out.println("Opens: " + descriptor.opens());
        System.out.println("Provides: " + descriptor.provides());
        System.out.println("Uses: " + descriptor.uses());
    }
}

Records (Java 14+) ​

java
// Basic record
public record Person(String name, int age) {
    // Compact constructor (executed before field assignment)
    public Person {
        if (age < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Age cannot be negative");
        }
    }
    
    // Instance method
    public boolean isAdult() {
        return age >= 18;
    }
    
    // Static method
    public static Person of(String name, int birthYear) {
        return new Person(name, java.time.Year.now().getValue() - birthYear);
    }
}

// Using records
public class RecordExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Creating record instances
        Person person1 = new Person("Alice", 30);
        Person person2 = new Person("Bob", 25);
        
        // Accessing components (automatically generated getters)
        System.out.println("Name: " + person1.name());
        System.out.println("Age: " + person1.age());
        
        // Using instance method
        System.out.println("Is adult: " + person1.isAdult());
        
        // Using static factory method
        Person person3 = Person.of("Charlie", 1990);
        System.out.println("Person 3: " + person3);
        
        // Records are immutable
        // person1.age = 31; // Compilation error
        
        // equals, hashCode, toString are automatically generated
        System.out.println("person1.equals(person2): " + person1.equals(person2));
        System.out.println("person1.hashCode(): " + person1.hashCode());
        System.out.println("person1.toString(): " + person1);
        
        // Deconstruction pattern matching (Java 16+ preview)
        if (person1 instanceof Person(String name, int age)) {
            System.out.println("Deconstructed: name=" + name + ", age=" + age);
        }
    }
}

// Record with validation
public record Email(String address) {
    public Email {
        if (address == null || !address.contains("@")) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid email address");
        }
    }
}

// Record with additional fields and methods
public record Employee(String id, String name, double salary) {
    // Static field
    private static final double MIN_SALARY = 30000.0;
    
    // Additional field (not part of the record components)
    private final String department;
    
    // Full constructor
    public Employee(String id, String name, double salary, String department) {
        this(id, name, salary); // Calls the canonical constructor
        this.department = department;
    }
    
    // Compact constructor
    public Employee {
        if (salary < MIN_SALARY) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Salary below minimum");
        }
    }
    
    // Accessor for additional field
    public String department() {
        return department;
    }
    
    // Additional method
    public double annualSalary() {
        return salary * 12;
    }
}

// Record implementing interfaces
public record Product(String code, String name, double price) implements Comparable<Product> {
    @Override
    public int compareTo(Product other) {
        return Double.compare(this.price, other.price);
    }
    
    // Override default method from interface
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return String.format("%s (%s): $%.2f", name, code, price);
    }
}

// Using records with collections
public class RecordCollectionExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Product> products = List.of(
            new Product("P001", "Laptop", 999.99),
            new Product("P002", "Phone", 699.99),
            new Product("P003", "Tablet", 399.99)
        );
        
        // Sorting records
        products.stream()
            .sorted()
            .forEach(System.out::println);
        
        // Filtering records
        products.stream()
            .filter(p -> p.price() > 500)
            .forEach(System.out::println);
        
        // Mapping records
        List<String> productNames = products.stream()
            .map(Product::name)
            .toList();
        
        System.out.println("Product names: " + productNames);
        
        // Using records as map keys
        Map<Product, Integer> inventory = new HashMap<>();
        inventory.put(new Product("P001", "Laptop", 999.99), 10);
        inventory.put(new Product("P002", "Phone", 699.99), 25);
        inventory.put(new Product("P003", "Tablet", 399.99), 15);
        
        inventory.forEach((product, quantity) -> 
            System.out.println(product + ": " + quantity + " units"));
    }
}

// Nested records
public record Order(String orderId, Customer customer, List<OrderItem> items) {
    public record Customer(String customerId, String name, String email) {
    }
    
    public record OrderItem(String productId, String productName, int quantity, double price) {
        public double totalPrice() {
            return quantity * price;
        }
    }
    
    public double orderTotal() {
        return items.stream()
            .mapToDouble(OrderItem::totalPrice)
            .sum();
    }
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Order.Customer customer = new Order.Customer("C001", "John Doe", "john@example.com");
        List<Order.OrderItem> items = List.of(
            new Order.OrderItem("P001", "Laptop", 1, 999.99),
            new Order.OrderItem("P002", "Mouse", 2, 25.99)
        );
        
        Order order = new Order("O001", customer, items);
        
        System.out.println("Order: " + order);
        System.out.println("Customer: " + order.customer());
        System.out.println("Items: " + order.items());
        System.out.println("Total: $" + order.orderTotal());
    }
}

// Record serialization
public record RecordSerializationExample implements Serializable {
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
    
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // Create a record
        Person person = new Person("Alice", 30);
        
        // Serialize to file
        try (ObjectOutputStream out = new ObjectOutputStream(
                new FileOutputStream("person.ser"))) {
            out.writeObject(person);
        }
        
        // Deserialize from file
        try (ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(
                new FileInputStream("person.ser"))) {
            Person deserializedPerson = (Person) in.readObject();
            System.out.println("Deserialized: " + deserializedPerson);
        }
    }
}

// Records vs. traditional classes
public class RecordComparison {
    // Traditional class implementation
    public static final class TraditionalPerson {
        private final String name;
        private final int age;
        
        public TraditionalPerson(String name, int age) {
            this.name = name;
            this.age = age;
        }
        
        public String getName() {
            return name;
        }
        
        public int getAge() {
            return age;
        }
        
        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object o) {
            if (this == o) return true;
            if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
            TraditionalPerson that = (TraditionalPerson) o;
            return age == that.age && Objects.equals(name, that.name);
        }
        
        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            return Objects.hash(name, age);
        }
        
        @Override
        public String toString() {
            return "TraditionalPerson{name='" + name + "', age=" + age + "}";
        }
    }
    
    // Record implementation (much more concise)
    public record RecordPerson(String name, int age) {}
    
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        TraditionalPerson traditional = new TraditionalPerson("Alice", 30);
        RecordPerson record = new RecordPerson("Alice", 30);
        
        System.out.println("Traditional: " + traditional);
        System.out.println("Record: " + record);
        
        // Both have the same behavior
        System.out.println("Traditional equals Record: " + 
            traditional.equals(new RecordPerson("Alice", 30))); // false, different types
        
        System.out.println("Record equals Record: " + 
            record.equals(new RecordPerson("Alice", 30))); // true
    }
}

Pattern Matching (Java 14+) ​

java
// instanceof pattern matching (Java 14+)
public class InstanceofPatternMatching {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Object obj = "Hello, World!";
        
        // Traditional instanceof
        if (obj instanceof String) {
            String str = (String) obj;
            System.out.println("String length: " + str.length());
        }
        
        // Pattern matching with instanceof
        if (obj instanceof String str) {
            System.out.println("String length: " + str.length());
        }
        
        // Pattern matching with additional conditions
        if (obj instanceof String str && str.length() > 5) {
            System.out.println("Long string: " + str);
        }
    }
}

// Switch expressions with pattern matching (Java 17+ preview, Java 21+ standard)
public class SwitchPatternMatching {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Object obj = 42;
        
        // Switch with type patterns
        String type = switch (obj) {
            case String s -> "String: " + s;
            case Integer i -> "Integer: " + i;
            case Double d -> "Double: " + d;
            default -> "Unknown: " + obj.getClass().getSimpleName();
        };
        
        System.out.println(type);
        
        // Switch with guarded patterns
        String result = switch (obj) {
            case String s when s.length() > 10 -> "Long string: " + s;
            case String s -> "Short string: " + s;
            case Integer i when i > 100 -> "Large integer: " + i;
            case Integer i -> "Small integer: " + i;
            default -> "Other type";
        };
        
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

// Record patterns (Java 19+ preview, Java 21+ standard)
public class RecordPatterns {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Using record patterns
        Object obj = new Point(10, 20);
        
        // Record pattern
        if (obj instanceof Point(int x, int y)) {
            System.out.println("Point coordinates: x=" + x + ", y=" + y);
        }
        
        // Nested record patterns
        Object nestedObj = new Circle(new Point(5, 5), 10);
        
        if (nestedObj instanceof Circle(Point(int x, int y), int radius)) {
            System.out.println("Circle at (" + x + ", " + y + ") with radius " + radius);
        }
        
        // Using record patterns in switch
        String shapeDescription = switch (obj) {
            case Point(int x, int y) -> "Point at (" + x + ", " + y + ")";
            case Circle(Point(int x, int y), int r) -> "Circle at (" + x + ", " + y + ") with radius " + r;
            default -> "Unknown shape";
        };
        
        System.out.println(shapeDescription);
    }
    
    record Point(int x, int y) {}
    record Circle(Point center, int radius) {}
}

Sealed Classes (Java 17+) ​

java
// Defining sealed classes
public sealed interface Shape 
    permits Circle, Rectangle, Triangle {
    
    double area();
    double perimeter();
}

// Implementations must be final, sealed, or non-sealed
final class Circle implements Shape {
    private final double radius;
    
    public Circle(double radius) {
        this.radius = radius;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double area() {
        return Math.PI * radius * radius;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double perimeter() {
        return 2 * Math.PI * radius;
    }
}

// Sealed class with permitted subclass
sealed class Rectangle implements Shape permits Square {
    private final double width;
    private final double height;
    
    public Rectangle(double width, double height) {
        this.width = width;
        this.height = height;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double area() {
        return width * height;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double perimeter() {
        return 2 * (width + height);
    }
}

// Final subclass
final class Square extends Rectangle {
    public Square(double side) {
        super(side, side);
    }
}

// Non-sealed subclass (allows further extension)
non-sealed class Triangle implements Shape {
    private final double a, b, c;
    
    public Triangle(double a, double b, double c) {
        this.a = a;
        this.b = b;
        this.c = c;
    }
    
    @Override
    public double area() {
        double s = (a + b + c) / 2;
        return Math.sqrt(s * (s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c));
    }
    
    @Override
    public double perimeter() {
        return a + b + c;
    }
}

// Using sealed classes with pattern matching
public class SealedClassExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Shape> shapes = List.of(
            new Circle(5),
            new Rectangle(4, 6),
            new Square(3)
        );
        
        for (Shape shape : shapes) {
            // Exhaustive pattern matching with sealed classes
            String description = switch (shape) {
                case Circle c -> "Circle with radius " + c.radius();
                case Rectangle r && !(r instanceof Square) -> 
                    "Rectangle with width " + r.width() + " and height " + r.height();
                case Square s -> "Square with side " + s.side();
            };
            
            System.out.println("Description: " + description);
        }
    }
}

Java 21 New Features ​

java
// Virtual Threads (Project Loom)
public class VirtualThreadsExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        // Creating a virtual thread
        Thread virtualThread = Thread.startVirtualThread(() -> {
            System.out.println("Running in a virtual thread: " + Thread.currentThread());
            try {
                Thread.sleep(1000);
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            }
            System.out.println("Virtual thread finished");
        });
        
        // Wait for virtual thread to complete
        virtualThread.join();
        
        // Using ExecutorService with virtual threads
        try (ExecutorService executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            // Submit tasks
            List<Future<String>> futures = new ArrayList<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
                final int taskId = i;
                Future<String> future = executor.submit(() -> {
                    Thread.sleep(100); // Simulate work
                    return "Task " + taskId + " completed by " + Thread.currentThread();
                });
                futures.add(future);
            }
            
            // Get results
            for (Future<String> future : futures) {
                System.out.println(future.get());
            }
        } catch (ExecutionException e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        }
    }
}

// Sequenced Collections (Java 21)
public class SequencedCollectionsExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // List is a SequencedCollection
        List<String> list = new ArrayList<>(List.of("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"));
        
        // Get first and last elements
        System.out.println("First element: " + list.getFirst()); // A
        System.out.println("Last element: " + list.getLast());   // E
        
        // Add to beginning and end
        list.addFirst("Z");
        list.addLast("F");
        System.out.println("Modified list: " + list); // [Z, A, B, C, D, E, F]
        
        // Remove from beginning and end
        String first = list.removeFirst(); // Z
        String last = list.removeLast();   // F
        System.out.println("Removed: " + first + ", " + last);
        System.out.println("Final list: " + list); // [A, B, C, D, E]
        
        // Get reversed view
        SequencedCollection<String> reversed = list.reversed();
        System.out.println("Reversed view: " + reversed); // [E, D, C, B, A]
        
        // LinkedHashSet is a SequencedSet
        SequencedSet<String> set = new LinkedHashSet<>(List.of("X", "Y", "Z"));
        System.out.println("First in set: " + set.getFirst()); // X
        System.out.println("Last in set: " + set.getLast());   // Z
        
        // LinkedHashMap is a SequencedMap
        SequencedMap<String, Integer> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        map.put("One", 1);
        map.put("Two", 2);
        map.put("Three", 3);
        
        System.out.println("First key: " + map.firstKey());   // One
        System.out.println("Last key: " + map.lastKey());     // Three
        
        map.putFirst("Zero", 0);
        map.putLast("Four", 4);
        System.out.println("Modified map: " + map); // {Zero=0, One=1, Two=2, Three=3, Four=4}
        
        String firstKey = map.pollFirstKey(); // Zero
        String lastKey = map.pollLastKey();   // Four
        System.out.println("Polled keys: " + firstKey + ", " + lastKey);
        System.out.println("Final map: " + map); // {One=1, Two=2, Three=3}
        
        // Get reversed view of map
        SequencedMap<String, Integer> reversedMap = map.reversed();
        System.out.println("Reversed map: " + reversedMap); // {Three=3, Two=2, One=1}
    }
}

// String Templates (Preview in Java 21)
public class StringTemplatesExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Basic string templates
        String name = "Alice";
        int age = 30;
        
        // Traditional string concatenation
        String message1 = "My name is " + name + " and I am " + age + " years old.";
        
        // Using String.format
        String message2 = String.format("My name is %s and I am %d years old.", name, age);
        
        // Using text blocks (Java 15+)
        String message3 = """
            My name is %s and I am %d years old.
            """.formatted(name, age);
        System.out.println(message3);
        
        // More complex template example with text blocks
        String json = """
            {
                "name": "%s",
                "age": %d,
                "adult": %b
            }
            """.formatted(name, age >= 18);
        System.out.println(json);
        
        // Using formatted for complex strings
        String formatted = "Name: %-10s | Age: %03d%n".formatted(name, age);
        System.out.print(formatted);
    }
}
